x_lr_adult: The other $43$ percent comes in adult life, from two sources. About $11$ percent of the whole gain, $26$ percent of the adult part, is the better productivity a child draws when its own parent does not carry the disorder. Escaping the penalty is worth a lot to each child it spares, about $12$ times what the average child gains at the same productivity, but it spares few children: the share of newborns who enter adult life with the penalty, because their parent carried a SUD, falls only from $8.99$ to $6.07$ percent. The remaining $32$ percent of the whole gain is that adult life is worth more at the same productivity, mainly because a household that stays clean is $42$ percent more likely to draw a voucher, paid for by the users the screen takes out of the programme and by the taxes that higher earnings bring in, and because the drug is $14$ percent cheaper. It is worth most to households that enter adult life with low productivity, who are the likeliest to need a voucher, so it is larger for a child whose own parent carried the disorder, whom the penalty leaves with lower productivity.
